content: Water says to the dirty: 'Come here.' The dirty says: 'I am ashamed.' Water says: 'How will you be cleansed without me?'
author: Rumi
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Most human unhappiness exists in two places that don't currently exist: the past, which cannot be changed, and the future, which hasn't happened yet. Meanwhile, the only life you will ever experience is slipping past unnoticed.

Across his life and work, Rumi saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Presence is not a rare mystical achievement; it is simply having the courtesy to show up for your own life. When you anchor your awareness in the immediate room and task, the frantic anxieties of the ego dissolve.
reflectionPrompt: What quiet yearning in your heart is asking for your attention and honest devotion?
